citations.finding: On the narrowest reading (Service Category 'Roads' only, without Neighbourhood Renewal and without the bridges) the total is 1,116,532 thousand, 11.2 times $100 million, below the $1.5 billion threshold. Neighbourhood Renewal profiles (722,289) fund whole-neighbourhood reconstruction including sidewalks, alleys and streetlights, and CM-25-0000 alone is 545,717; whether all of that is 'roads' is a labelling choice.
citations.establishes: That the Supported classification depends on counting Neighbourhood Renewal as roads; excluding it gives Partially supported.
citations.quote: Service Category: Neighbourhood Renewal

citations.finding: The $1,794.0 million 'Active Pathways and Roads Service' line that matches the councillor's '$1.8 billion' contains CM-20-0330 (100,000) and the other active-pathway and streetscape profiles (for example Missing and Enhanced Sidewalk Connections 13,615; Edmonton-Strathcona County Pedestrian Bridge 30,205; 103A Avenue Pedway 25,400; 170 Street Pedestrian Bridge 471), so as a 'roads' figure it double counts the bike money it is being compared with.
citations.establishes: That the combined service line is not a roads-only total; the roads-only total under the City's labels is nonetheless higher (1,945.7 million) because the bridges and Neighbourhood Renewal profiles listed under other asset categories are included.

items.title: Budget minutes item 13.18 (Operating Budget Amendment 18); 2023-2026 Operating Budget and Plans pp.23 and 105-106

citations.finding: In December 2022 council funded the Enhanced Snow and Ice Control Service Standards package at 20 per cent: 2023 $274,600 (Community Standards) plus $3,768,000 (Parks and Roads); 2024 $3,724,800; 2025 $2,476,800; 2026 $721,400, Carried 12 to 1 (Janz opposed). The Operating Budget document prints the package at $4,043K (2023), $3,725K (2024), $2,477K (2025), $721K (2026) and summarises it as '$11.0 million for enhanced snow and ice control'.
citations.establishes: The 2023-2026 snow enhancement approved in the same deliberations; the Operating Budget document itself publishes Snow and Ice Control only inside the Parks and Roads Services branch totals, not as a program line.
citations.quote: $11.0 million for enhanced snow and ice control.

citations.finding: The 2022 Adjusted Budget gross expenditure for Snow and Ice Control was $56.6 million (Net expenditure + revenue). The 2023 approved gross budget was $57.4 million.
citations.establishes: The approved 2022 and 2023 snow clearing budgets.

items.title: Global News, 'City council hearing mixed reaction on $100 million to Edmonton bike plan' (Stephanie Swensrude)

citations.finding: Global News quoted Councillor Michael Janz on 2022-12-12: 'Only $100 million is going to bike lanes but $1.8 billion, 180 times as much, is going towards roads.' The same outlet reported on 2022-12-09 that council approved $100 million for bike infrastructure over four years by a 9-4 vote.
citations.establishes: The circulating form and that the record has '180', not '18' (2022-12-09 article: https://globalnews.ca/news/9338993/edmonton-city-council-100-million-bike-lanes).
citations.quote: Only $100 million is going to bike lanes but $1.8 billion, 180 times as much, is going towards roads.

citations.finding: Global News recorded the councillor saying '$1.8 billion, 180 times as much.' The two dollar figures imply 18 times, not 180.
citations.establishes: The quotation's arithmetic discrepancy, not any budget amount.

items.title: FCS02852 Attachment 4 Spring 2025 SCBA Budget Adjustments (p.1); FCS03313 Attachment 2 Significant Capital Project Update as of December 31, 2025
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Financial and Corporate Services

citations.finding: The profile budgets have moved since adoption. The Spring 2025 Supplemental Capital Budget Adjustment (approved 2025-06-10) transferred $430,000 of Tax-Supported Debt ($20,000 in 2025, $410,000 in 2026) out of CM-20-0330 into the new standalone profile 25-25-9506 Dunluce Neighbourhood and Alley Renewal, reducing CM-20-0330 to 99,570; the Capital Financial Updates for 2025-09-30 and 2025-12-31 show its Current Approved Budget at 99,570. No other amendment to CM-20-0330 was found in the Spring 2023, Fall 2023, Spring 2024, Fall 2024, Spring 2025 or Fall 2025 adjustments. Roads profiles changed more: the Capital Financial Update as of 2025-12-31 shows Terwillegar Drive (19-22-9006) with a total profile budget of 327,220 against an original 102,700, and 50 Street CPR Grade Separation (18-66-6503) 181,508 against 86,600 (total-profile figures, not 2023-2026 only), while composite renewal profiles show smaller current budgets (CM-22-0000 29,492; CM-24-0000 56,078; CM-25-0000 48,522) because work was split into standalone profiles.
citations.establishes: The only amendment to CM-20-0330 (-$430K, 2025-06-10) and that a roads-only 2023-2026 total as amended cannot be rebuilt from the published summaries because composite profiles were split and multi-cycle profiles are reported life-to-date. items.title: 2022 Budget Highlights, '2022 Operating Budget Changes' (PDF p.101, printed p.98); CO01733 Snow and Ice Control 2022-23 Winter Season Results, p.3

citations.finding: Council's Spring 2022 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment added $14,300 thousand one-time to Parks and Roads Services for 'Enhanced Snow Clearing Pilot costs (total costs of $16.6 M, less $2.3M from 2021 program surplus approved by Council on March 14, 2022)', funded by transfer from the Financial Stabilization Reserve; CO01733 records a further one-time $4.7 million approved 2022-07-04. These one-time additions explain most of the gap between the base 2022 budget (63,666) and the amended year-end budget (79,474).
citations.establishes: That the 2022 budget in force in December 2022 included roughly $19 million of one-time, reserve-funded snow money, so the 'in force' and 'base approved' readings of the primary denominator differ.

items.title: Global News, 'Major changes to Edmonton snow clearing not expected following budget cut: city'; CBC News, 'What got funded, and what didn't, in Edmonton city council's budget debate'

citations.finding: Media at the time reported the snow budget in net terms close to the City's net figures: Global News (2022-12-20) 'base snow and ice funding, $63.6 million' plus $4.7 million for 2022 and 'The total amount of money going towards snow and ice removal in 2023 will be $60.9 million'; CBC (2022-12-20) 'The total budget for snow clearing was just under $62 million' for 2022 and $56.9 million set for 2023 before the $4 million increase.
citations.establishes: Only that contemporaneous reporting put the annual snow budget at roughly $57-64 million, consistent with the base figures above and inconsistent with any denominator near $50 million that 'almost double' would need (CBC: https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/what-got-funded-and-what-didn-t-in-edmonton-city-council-s-budget-debate-1.6691557).
citations.quote: The total amount of money going towards snow and ice removal in 2023 will be $60.9 million.

items.title: Common Sense Edmonton, 'Stop The Bike Lane Boondoggle' (Wayback capture 2022-12-12 05:58:23 and live page)

citations.finding: The advocacy page, captured by the Wayback Machine on 2022-12-12 and still live on 2026-09-02, says: 'spending $100 million on more bike lanes'; 'the $100 million he wants to spend on Bike Lanes is almost 5 times the amount he wants to spend on affordable housing'; 'In fact, it's almost double the City's annual snow-clearing budget!' It gives no snow figure and no source, and describes the $100 million as 'approved as an amendment to the budget by a 9-4 vote on Friday'.
citations.establishes: The holder's exact wording and that no denominator was stated; nothing establishes use of the proposed 2023 figure. The page lists petition signers' names, which are not reproduced here.
citations.quote: In fact, it's almost double the City's annual snow-clearing budget!
